question.text: A Large Value Fund (LVF) classified as a Category III AIF enjoys a relaxed concentration limit for single investee company, which is:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 10.1.4.1: SEBI relaxes Cat III concentration limit to 20% of Investable Funds or NAV for LVFs (vs 10% for regular Cat III). LVF = minimum INR 70 cr investor commitment per investor. **The Trap:** A is the regular limit. B, D are fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C same. XIX-D: Cat I/II LVF has different relaxations. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** LVF election is disclosed in PPM; once elected, you cannot reverse without investor consent. Don't elect LVF unless genuinely running concentrated activist book — the 20% cap is useless otherwise and restricts investor base to ultra-HNI (INR 70 cr each).
